title: Which numbers leave remainder one on division by two and by three?
description: Numbers are tested for remainder one on division by two and by three, and the matches are written with one letter-number. Keeko's doubt is that five k plus one must fit, because two and three make five.
teaching_notes: One idea: take the common remainder away, and what is left is a multiple of both divisors. Watch for students who add the two divisors instead of finding a number that both divide.

source: Find numbers that leave remainder 1 on division by 2 and rem
video_script.why: The student can already write numbers with a given remainder and now finds numbers that leave the same remainder on division by two different numbers.
video_script.substitution: Remainder one on division by two and by three, with the numbers one to thirteen listed first.
video_script.anchor: dots grouped in twos and in threes with one dot left over each time, the picture of the What Remains part of the book
video_script.wrong_answer: the numbers are five k plus one
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the divisors two and three to get five without testing; k equal to one gives six, which leaves remainder zero on division by two and by three.
video_script.payoff_line: All numbers of the form six k plus one fit

final_answer.spoken: one, seven, thirteen, nineteen and so on, all of the form six k plus one

maths_rules: odd numbers 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 leave remainder 1 on division by 2
1 - 1 = 0, 7 - 1 = 6, 13 - 1 = 12 are multiples of 2 and of 3, so multiples of 6
5k + 1 at k = 1: 6 = 2 x 3 + 0, remainder 0 on division by 2
video_script.design: One strip of the numbers one to thirteen. The matches light up step by step, then the numbers one less are shown as multiples of six.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book, What Remains; the numbers 1 to 13 on a strip; the words remainder 1 on division by 2 and remainder 1 on division by 3

marks.ask: the strip of numbers appears with the two conditions written above it
marks.which: a question mark and the words one expression appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, in the part called What Remains.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>A number leaves remainder one on division by two, and remainder one on division by three.
<bookmark mark='which'/>Which numbers are these, and can one expression give all of them?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 13 dots as 6 pairs and 1 loose; the same 13 dots as 4 threes and 1 loose

marks.pairs: thirteen dots fall into six pairs with one dot loose
marks.threes: the same thirteen dots regroup into four threes with one dot loose

narration: <bookmark mark='pairs'/>Thirteen dots in pairs make six pairs, with one dot left.
<bookmark mark='threes'/>The same thirteen dots in threes make four threes, with one dot left.
A remainder is what is left after making full groups.

beats.on_screen: Given: remainder 1 on division by 2 and remainder 1 on division by 3
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a number leaves remainder one on division by two and remainder one on division by three.

beats.on_screen: To find: these numbers, and one expression for all of them

marks.find: the two things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find these numbers and write one expression for all of them.

marks.odd: the odd numbers on the strip light up
marks.list: the seven odd numbers are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='odd'/>Step one, list the numbers that leave remainder one on division by two.
These are the odd numbers.
<bookmark mark='list'/>One, three, five, seven, nine, eleven and thirteen.

marks.test: each odd number is divided by three in turn
marks.thirteen: thirteen is shown as four threes and one over
marks.others: three, five, nine and eleven turn grey with remainders zero, two, zero and two

narration: <bookmark mark='test'/>Step two, which of these leave remainder one on division by three?
One is three times zero plus one.
Seven is three times two plus one.
<bookmark mark='thirteen'/>Thirteen is three times four plus one.
<bookmark mark='others'/>Three, five, nine and eleven leave remainder zero, two, zero and two.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: take 1 away: 1 - 1 = 0, 7 - 1 = 6, 13 - 1 = 12; multiples of 2 and of 3, so of 6

marks.take: one is taken away from each of the three numbers
marks.mult: zero, six and twelve are marked as multiples of two and of three
marks.six: the words multiples of six appear

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step three, take one away from each of these three numbers.
One, seven and thirteen become zero, six and twelve.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>These are multiples of two and also multiples of three.
<bookmark mark='six'/>That makes them multiples of six.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: a multiple of 6, plus 1: 6k + 1; k = 0, 1, 2, 3 gives 1, 7, 13, 19

marks.form: a multiple of six plus one is written as six k plus one
marks.vals: k equal to zero, one, two and three give one, seven, thirteen and nineteen

narration: <bookmark mark='form'/>Step four, each number is a multiple of six, plus one.
We write this as six k plus one.
<bookmark mark='vals'/>Putting in k as zero, one, two and three gives one, seven, thirteen and nineteen.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 1, 7, 13, 19, and so on: all numbers of the form 6k + 1
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The numbers are one, seven, thirteen, nineteen and so on.
All numbers of the form six k plus one fit.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the strip of numbers
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 5k + 1 with k = 1 giving 6; 6 = 2 x 3 + 0 and 6 = 3 x 2 + 0, so 6 does not fit

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows five k plus one
marks.test: k equal to one gives six, and six is split into three pairs
marks.fix: six is split into two threes, and a cross appears on the card

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the numbers are five k plus one, because two and three make five.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Put k equal to one, and five k plus one gives six.
Six leaves remainder zero on division by two.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>It also leaves remainder zero on division by three, so it does not fit.
